newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker with U.S. after ECI data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker with U.S. after ECI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened mostly weaker on Tuesday, taking direction from U.S. Treasuries following the release of U.S. employment cost index data, analysts said.

"The focus this morning was on the U.S. ECI but it really came out as a ho-hummer, on expectations. So there's maybe a little bit of profit-taking on that as the market awaits the more important data later on in the week," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.23 to C$120.34 to yield 6.454 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.42 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to three basis points from four basis points at Monday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets were weaker after the U.S. Labor Department said the employment cost index for the second quarter rose 0.8 percent, in line with expectations.
Analysts said fixed-income markets have now turned their attention to other major U.S. economic reports out this week, which include the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report for July out on Friday.
Canadian economic reports out this morning, including the industrial product and raw material price indicies has little impact on prices, analysts said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.08 to C$109.71 to yield 5.931 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.14 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 21 basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
